title: Bengal postpones voter-roll revision days before start, citing 'unavoidable circumstances'
dek: The Special Summary Revision of the rolls was to begin on 23 November. Reports link the delay to a backlog at the tribunals hearing appeals from voters dropped in the SIR.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer has postponed the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of the state's electoral rolls, which was due to begin on Monday, 23 November, citing "some unavoidable circumstances". A fresh schedule will be announced later, the office said on Friday, according to reports. It gave no other reason.

The SSR is the annual update of the voters' list, when the draft roll is published and people can apply to be added, object to names or correct their details. It is the first such revision in Bengal since the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Election Commission's door-to-door re-verification of voters that removed large numbers of names from the rolls before this year's Assembly election. The roll that comes out of it is expected to be used for the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections early next year.

## Why it was delayed

The CEO's office did not explain the "unavoidable circumstances". According to reports citing unnamed officials, the main problem is a backlog at the SIR appeal tribunals, which hear appeals from people who say they were wrongly removed from the rolls. Several tribunal members have resigned citing personal reasons, leaving the rest with a heavy workload, and some applicants have been slow to submit documents, the reports said. The applications and supporting documents of people left out of the final roll "are being scrutinised for inclusion", one official said, according to reports.

Reports also said that the revised rolls had not yet reached the state CEO's office from the Commission. The draft roll had originally been due on 20 November and was then moved to 23 November.

## What was planned

Under the schedule now on hold, claims and objections were to be filed from 23 November to 22 December, disposed of by 8 January, and the final roll published on 16 January 2027, according to reports. Some reports had given slightly different dates for the claims period earlier this month. There are now concerns that the final roll will be delayed, reports said.

Bengal is one of five states and union territories where the revision is under way, with Maharashtra, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, according to reports. Uttar Pradesh deferred its own draft roll earlier this month.

## The political stakes

The revision has been contested from the start. At an all-party meeting called by the CEO on 3 November, the Trinamool Congress, the Congress and the Left Front objected to new Election Commission rules on Form 7, which is used to seek the deletion of a name, saying it could be used to strike off genuine voters before the civic polls. They also demanded that voters excluded in the SIR be allowed to apply for inclusion. The BJP, which governs the state, defended the rules as a way to clean up the rolls.

None of the parties had publicly responded to the postponement by Saturday morning. Nationally, opposition parties have demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR, and are expected to raise it in the Winter Session of Parliament, which is likely to begin in the first week of December, according to reports.

## What happens next

The Election Commission is expected to announce a new schedule for Bengal's draft roll. Any long delay could push back the final roll, and with it the Kolkata and Howrah civic elections that Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has suggested could be held before Siliguri's, in February 2027.
